282.text: Which of the following is not a bioassay for cytokinins?
282.sol: Cytokinins have the ability to retard the degradation of chlorophyll in excised leaves. Hence, chlorophyll preservation test is a bioassay for cytokinin. Cytokinin promotes cell enlargement in the leaf tissues of certain plants. So, radish and bean leaf test have been used as bioassay. Promotion of lettuce seed germination forms the basis for another bioassay for cytokinins. Dwarf maize test is a bioassay for gibberellins as they induce internodal growth in genetically dwarf varieties of plants like pea and maize.

1855.text: Which of the following pairs does not have same dimensions ?
options: moment of inertia and moment of force
1855.sol:
Impulse $=F \times t$
$$
=\frac{m\left(v_2-v_1\right)}{t} \times t=m\left(v_2-v_1\right)
$$
$=$ change in momentum
$\therefore \quad$ [Impulse $]=[$ Momentum $]$
Angular momentum, $\mathrm{L}=m v r$
Planck's constant, $[h]=[$ energy $] \times[$ time $]$
$$
\Rightarrow[F \times r \times \text{ time })=\frac{m\left(v_2-v_1\right)}{t} \times r \times t
$$
$\Rightarrow m\left(v_2-v_1\right) \times r=($ change of momentum $) \times r$
$\therefore \quad[h]=[L]$.
Work, $W=\vec{F} \cdot \vec{d}:$ Torque, $\tau=\vec{r} \times \vec{F}$
$$
\therefore \quad[W]=[\tau]
$$
Moment of inertia, $I=m r^2=\operatorname{mass} \times(\text{ distance })^2$

Moment of force, $\tau=\vec{r} \times \vec{F}=$ distance $\times$ force
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \quad=\text{ distance } \times \frac{\text{ change of momentum }}{\text{ time }} \\
& \therefore \quad[\mathrm{I}] \neq[\tau] .
\end{aligned}
$$
Therefore, moment of inertia and moment of force have different dimensions.

1951.text: An artificial pacemaker is implanted subcutaneously and connected to the heart in patients
options: having $90 \%$ blockage of the three main coronary arteries
having a very high blood pressure
with irregularity in the heart rhythm
1951.sol: A pacemaker (or "artificial pacemaker"), is a medical device designed to regulate the beating of the heart. The purpose of an artificial pacemaker is to stimulate the heart when either the heart's native pacemaker is not fast enough or if there are blocks in the heart's electrical conduction system preventing the propagation of electrical impulses from the native pacemaker to the lower chambers of the heart, known as the ventricles. Generally, pacemakers do not treat fast rhythms of the heart.

7032.text: If the circles \((x+a)^2+(y+b)^2=a²\) and \((x+c)^2+(y+d)^2=d²\) cut orthogonally, then \(b(b-2 d)=\)
7032.sol:
Given equation of circles are
$\begin{aligned}
(x+a)^2+(y+b)^2 & =a² \\
\Rightarrow \quad x²+y²+2 a x+2 b y+b² & =0 \quad \ldots (i) \\
(x+c)^2+(y+d)^2 & =d² \\
\Rightarrow \quad x²+y²+2 c x+2 d y+c² & =0 \quad \ldots (ii)
\end{aligned}$ \)
From Eq. (i) \(g_1=a ; f_1=b, c_1=b²\)
From Eq. (ii) \(g_2=c ; f_2=d ; c_2=c²\)
If circles (i) and (ii) are orthogonal, $\begin{array}{rlrl}
\Rightarrow& & 2\left[g_1 g_2+f_1 f_2\right]& =c_1+c_2 \\
\Rightarrow & 2 & 2(a c+b d) & =b²+c² \\
& \Rightarrow & 2 a c+2 b d & =b²+c² \\
& \Rightarrow & 2 a c-c² & =b²-2 b d \\
& \Rightarrow & c(2 a-c) & =b(b-2 d) \\
& \therefore & b(b-2 d) & =c(2 a-c)
\end{array}$
\(\therefore\) Hence, answer is (b).

9377.subject: Mathematics
9377.sol:
Given:

$f\left(x\right) = ∫ {cosec}^{5}xdx$

        $= ∫ \mathop{\left({cosec}^{3}x\right)}_{\text{I}}\mathop{\left({cosec}^{2}x\right)}_{\text{II}}dx$

$= {cosec}^{3}x\left(- cotx\right) - ∫ \left\{\left(- 3{cosec}^{3}xcotx\right)\left(- cotx\right)\right\}dx$

$= - {cosec}^{3}xcotx - ∫ 3{cosec}^{3}x{cot}^{2}xdx$

$= - {cosec}^{3}xcotx - ∫ 3{cosec}^{3}x\left({cosec}^{2}x - 1\right)dx$

$= - {cosec}^{3}xcotx - 3 ∫ {cosec}^{5}xdx + 3 ∫ {cosec}^{3}xdx$

$= - {cosec}^{3}xcotx - 3f\left(x\right) + 3 ∫ {cosec}^{3}xdx$

$⇒ 4f\left(x\right) = - {cosec}^{3}xcotx + 3 ∫ {cosec}^{3}xdx$

$⇒ 4f\left(x\right) = - {cosec}^{3}xcotx + 3I . . . \left(i\right)$

Now,

$I = ∫ {cosec}^{3}xdx$

  $= ∫ \left(cosec x\right)\left({cosec}^{2}x\right)dx$

$= \left(cosec x\right) ∫ \left({cosec}^{2}x\right)dx - ∫ \left\{\left(- cosec xcotx\right)\left(- cotx\right)\right\}dx$

$= - cosec xcotx - ∫ \left(cosec x{cot}^{2}x\right)dx$

$= - cosec xcotx - ∫ cosec x\left({cosec}^{2}x - 1\right)dx$

$= - cosec xcotx - ∫ {cosec}^{3}xdx + ∫ cose\text{c}xdx$

$⇒ I = - cosec xcotx - I + ∫ cose\text{c}xdx$

$⇒ 2I = \left(- cosec xcotx\right) + log\left|cosec x - cotx\right| + C$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left\{\left(- cosec xcotx\right) + log\left|cosec x - cotx\right| + C\right\}$

Putting in $\left(i\right)$, we get

$⇒ 4f\left(x\right) = - {cosec}^{3}xcotx + \dfrac{3}{2}\left\{\left(- cosec xcotx\right) + log\left|cosec x - cotx\right|\right\} + c$

Putting $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ in above equation, we get

$⇒ 4f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = - {\left\{cosec \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right\}}^{3}cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) + \dfrac{3}{2}\left[\left\{- cosec \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right\} + log\left|cosec \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) - cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right|\right] + c '$

 $⇒ 4f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = - 2\sqrt{2} + \dfrac{3}{2}\left\{- \sqrt{2} + log\left|\sqrt{2} - 1\right|\right\} + c '$

$⇒ 4f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = - \dfrac{7\sqrt{2}}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2}\left(log\left|\sqrt{2} - 1\right|\right) + c '$

$⇒ 4f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = - \dfrac{7\sqrt{2}}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2}\left(log\left|\dfrac{\left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)\left(\sqrt{2} + 1\right)}{\left(\sqrt{2} + 1\right)}\right|\right) + c '$

$⇒ 4f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = - \dfrac{7\sqrt{2}}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2}\left\{log\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2} + 1}\right)\right\} + c '$

$⇒ 4f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = - \dfrac{7\sqrt{2}}{2} - \dfrac{3}{2}\left\{log\left(\sqrt{2} + 1\right)\right\} + c '$

$⇒ f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = - \dfrac{1}{8}\left[7\sqrt{2} + 3\left\{log\left(\sqrt{2} + 1\right)\right\}\right] + c$.

Box contains 4 defective and 6 good machines.

Probability that both machines are good

12991.text:
Let \(\alpha, \beta\) and \(\gamma\) be such that \(0 < \alpha < \beta < \gamma <2 \pi\).
For any \(x \in \mathbb{R}\) if \(\cos (x+\alpha)+\cos (x+\beta)+\cos (x+\gamma)=0 \text{, }\)
then \(\tan (\gamma-\alpha)=\)
12991.sol:
It is given that for any \(x \in \mathbb{R}\).
\(\cos (x+\alpha)+\cos (x+\beta)+\cos (x+\gamma)=0\)
Now, put \(x=-\alpha-\beta-\gamma\),
\(0  <  \alpha <  \beta <  \gamma <2 \pi\), we get
$$\begin{aligned}& \cos (\beta+\gamma)+\cos (\alpha+\gamma)+\cos (\alpha+\beta)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 2 \cos \left(\frac{\alpha+2 \beta+\gamma}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{\gamma-\alpha}{2}\right)+\cos (\alpha+\gamma)=0 \quad \ldots (i)
\end{aligned} \)
Now, put \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}-\beta\), we get
 \begin{array}{ll}& \sin (\beta-\alpha)+\sin (\beta-\gamma)=0 \\
\Rightarrow & \sin (\beta-\alpha)=\sin (\gamma-\beta)\\
\Rightarrow \quad & 2 \beta=\alpha+\gamma \quad \ldots (ii)
\end{array}$$\)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$$\begin{array}{rc}& \cos(\alpha+\gamma)\left[\frac{1}{2} \cos \left(\frac{\gamma-\alpha}{2}\right)+1\right]=0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad & \quad \cos\left(\frac{\gamma-\alpha}{2}\right)=-\frac{1}{2} \\
\Rightarrow \quad & \frac{\gamma-\alpha}{2}=\frac{2 \pi}{3} \Rightarrow \gamma-\alpha=\frac{\pi}{3}
\end{array}$$\)
So, \(\tan (\gamma-\alpha)=\sqrt{3}\)

15405.text:
Statement (A): When the temperature increases the viscosity of gases increases and the viscosity of liquids decreases.

Statement (B): Water does not wet an oily glass because cohesive force of oil is less than that of water.

Statement (C) : A liquid will wet a surface of a solid if the angle of contact is greater than $90 °$.

C is true
B and C false, A is true

15405.sol:
Statement A:

In liquid: With the rise in temperature, viscosity of a liquid decreases because the intermolecular attractive force between consecutive layers decreases as temperature increases.&

In gasses: The important cause of viscosity is randomness/molecular collision due to root mean square& velocity. Due to rise in temperature, kinetic energy of molecules increases which makes rms velocity increase, hence randomness and collision of molecules increases. This makes the flow difficult& and hence viscosity in gasses increases with temperature.

Statement B:

Water does not wet an oily glass, because & cohesive force for water > adhesive force between water and oil molecules.

Statement C:

When the liquid does not wet the sides of a solid object, it means that the angle of contact is more than $90 °$ but less than $180 °$.

17234.text: A block of mass $m=25 \mathrm{ kg}$ sliding on a smooth horizontal surface with a velocity $v=3 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$ meets the spring of spring constant $k=100 \mathrm{ N} / \mathrm{m}$ fixed at one end as shown in figure. The maximum compression of the spring and velocity of block as it returns to the original position respectively are
17234.sol:
When block strikes the spring, the kinetic energy of block converts into potential energy of spring ie,
$\frac{1}{2} m v^2=\frac{1}{2} k x^2$
where $x$ is compression in spring.
$x=\sqrt{\frac{m v^2}{k}}=\sqrt{\frac{25 \times(3)^2}{100}}=\sqrt{\frac{9}{4}}=\frac{3}{2}=1.5 \mathrm{ m}$
When block returns to the original position, again potential energy converts into kinetic energy of the block, so velocity of the block is same as before but its sign changes as it goes to mean position.
Hence, $\quad v=-3 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$.

20626.subject: Chemistry
20626.text: At $298 \mathrm{~K}, \mathrm{CO}_2$ exerts a partial pressure of 0.835 bar. The amount of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ in millimoles dissolved in 0.9 L of water is: $\left[\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{H}}\right.$ for $\mathrm{CO}_2$ at 298 K is $\left.1.67 \times 10^3 \mathrm{bar}\right]$
20626.sol:
Henry's Law states that the partial pressure of a gas is proportional to its mole fraction in the solution: $P = K_H \times \chi$.

Given $P = 0.835 \text{ bar}$ and $K_H = 1.67 \times 10^3 \text{ bar}$, the mole fraction $\chi$ of $\text{CO}_2$ is calculated as:

$\chi = \dfrac{P}{K_H} = \dfrac{0.835}{1.67 \times 10^3} = 0.5 \times 10^{-3} = 5 \times 10^{-4}$.

The mole fraction $\chi$ is defined as $\chi = \dfrac{n_{\text{CO}_2}}{n_{\text{CO}_2} + n_{\text{H}_2\text{O}}}$. Since the amount of dissolved gas is very small, $n_{\text{CO}_2} + n_{\text{H}_2\text{O}} \approx n_{\text{H}_2\text{O}}$.

The number of moles of water in $0.9 \text{ L}$ is $n_{\text{H}_2\text{O}} = \dfrac{900 \text{ g}}{18 \text{ g/mol}} = 50 \text{ mol}$.

Therefore, $n_{\text{CO}_2} = \chi \times n_{\text{H}_2\text{O}} = 5 \times 10^{-4} \times 50 = 250 \times 10^{-4} = 0.025 \text{ mol}$.

Converting to millimoles: $0.025 \text{ mol} = 25 \text{ mmol}$.

Answer: 25 mmol

20658.subject: Chemistry
20658.text:
The boiling point of a $4 \%$ aqueous solution of a non-volatile solute $\mathrm{P}$ is equal to the boiling point of $\mathrm{X} \%$ solution of another non-volatile solute $\mathrm{Q}$.
The relation between their Molar masses is $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{Q}}=4 \mathrm{ Mp}$. What is $\mathrm{X}$ ?
20658.sol:
The elevation in boiling point is given by $\Delta T_b = K_b \times m$, where $m$ is the molality of the solution. Since the boiling points of the two solutions are equal, their elevations in boiling point are equal, which implies their molalities must be equal, assuming the solvent is the same and the solutes are non-volatile and non-electrolytic.

Let $w_P$ and $w_Q$ be the masses of solutes P and Q in $100 \text{ g}$ of solution. For a $4 \%$ solution of P, $w_P = 4 \text{ g}$ and the mass of solvent is $100 - 4 = 96 \text{ g}$. The molality $m_P$ is given by $m_P = \dfrac{w_P / M_P}{W_{solvent, P} / 1000} = \dfrac{4 / M_P}{96 / 1000} = \dfrac{4000}{96 M_P} = \dfrac{125}{3 M_P}$.

For an $X \%$ solution of Q, $w_Q = X \text{ g}$ and the mass of solvent is $100 - X \text{ g}$. The molality $m_Q$ is given by $m_Q = \dfrac{X / M_Q}{(100 - X) / 1000} = \dfrac{1000 X}{(100 - X) M_Q}$.

Equating $m_P$ and $m_Q$: $\dfrac{125}{3 M_P} = \dfrac{1000 X}{(100 - X) M_Q}$.

Given $M_Q = 4 M_P$, substitute this into the equation: $\dfrac{125}{3 M_P} = \dfrac{1000 X}{(100 - X) (4 M_P)}$.

Simplifying: $\dfrac{125}{3} = \dfrac{250 X}{100 - X} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{2 X}{100 - X} \Rightarrow 100 - X = 6 X \Rightarrow 7 X = 100 \Rightarrow X = \dfrac{100}{7} \approx 14.2857$.

Rounding to two decimal places, $X = 14.29$.

Answer: 14.29

20701.subject: Chemistry
20701.text: When one mole of a hydrocarbon $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{a}} \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{b}}$ undergoes complete combustion, it requires 7.5 moles of $\mathrm{O}_2$ and results in the production of 6 moles of $\mathrm{CO}_2$. Calculate the values of $\mathrm{a}$ and $\mathrm{b}$.
20701.sol:
The combustion reaction of a hydrocarbon $C_{a}H_{b}$ is given by the equation:

$C_{a}H_{b} + (a + \dfrac{b}{4})O_{2} \rightarrow aCO_{2} + \dfrac{b}{2}H_{2}O$

Given that 6 moles of $CO_{2}$ are produced from 1 mole of hydrocarbon, we have $a = 6$.

Given that 7.5 moles of $O_{2}$ are required for complete combustion, we have the stoichiometric coefficient for oxygen:

$a + \dfrac{b}{4} = 7.5$

Substituting $a = 6$ into the equation:

$6 + \dfrac{b}{4} = 7.5$

$\dfrac{b}{4} = 7.5 - 6 = 1.5$

$b = 1.5 \times 4 = 6$

Therefore, $a = 6$ and $b = 6$.

Answer: $a=6$ and $b=6$

21132.text:
$S \equiv x^2+y^2+2 x+3 y+1=0$ and
$S^{\prime} \equiv x^2+y^2+4 x+3 y+2=0$ are two circles.
The point $(-3,-2)$ lies
21132.sol:
Let $S(x, y) = x^2 + y^2 + 2x + 3y + 1$ and $S'(x, y) = x^2 + y^2 + 4x + 3y + 2$.

To determine the position of the point $P(-3,-2)$ with respect to the circles, we evaluate the power of the point for each circle.

For circle $S$:
$S(-3,-2) = (-3)^2 + (-2)^2 + 2(-3) + 3(-2) + 1$
$S(-3,-2) = 9 + 4 - 6 - 6 + 1 = 2$.
Since $S(-3,-2) > 0$, the point $(-3,-2)$ lies outside circle $S$.

For circle $S'$:
$S'(-3,-2) = (-3)^2 + (-2)^2 + 4(-3) + 3(-2) + 2$
$S'(-3,-2) = 9 + 4 - 12 - 6 + 2 = -3$.
Since $S'(-3,-2) < 0$, the point $(-3,-2)$ lies inside circle $S'$.

Therefore, the point lies inside $S'$ only.

Answer: inside $S^{\prime}$ only

21531.sol:
Let $L = \lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \dfrac{(\sqrt{x}-1)(2 x-3)}{2 x^2+x-3}$.

Factor the denominator: $2x^2 + x - 3 = 2x^2 + 3x - 2x - 3 = x(2x + 3) - 1(2x + 3) = (x - 1)(2x + 3)$.

Substitute the factored form into the limit expression:

$L = \lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \dfrac{(\sqrt{x}-1)(2 x-3)}{(x-1)(2x+3)}$

Since $x - 1 = (\sqrt{x} - 1)(\sqrt{x} + 1)$, the expression becomes:

$L = \lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \dfrac{(\sqrt{x}-1)(2 x-3)}{(\sqrt{x}-1)(\sqrt{x}+1)(2x+3)}$

Cancel the common term $(\sqrt{x}-1)$:

$L = \lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \dfrac{2x-3}{(\sqrt{x}+1)(2x+3)}$

Evaluate the limit by substituting $x = 1$:

$L = \dfrac{2(1)-3}{(\sqrt{1}+1)(2(1)+3)} = \dfrac{2-3}{(1+1)(2+3)} = \dfrac{-1}{2 \times 5} = -\dfrac{1}{10}$

Answer: $-\dfrac{1}{10}$

23522.subject: Physics
23522.text: A block of metal A is connected in series with another block of metal B such that the two metal blocks have the same area of cross sections. The thermal conductivity of metal A is K and the free end of metal A is at $80^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$. The temperature of the interface is $60^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ and the free end of metal B is at $20^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$. Assuming the two metals have the same thickness, the conductivity of metal B is:
23522.sol:
In a steady state, the rate of heat flow through two blocks connected in series is the same. Let $A$ be the cross-sectional area and $L$ be the thickness of each block. The rate of heat flow $H$ is given by $H = \dfrac{KA(T_1 - T_2)}{L}$.

For metal A, the temperature difference is $80^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C} - 60^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C} = 20^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$. Thus, $H_A = \dfrac{KA(80 - 60)}{L} = \dfrac{20KA}{L}$.

For metal B, let $K_B$ be its thermal conductivity. The temperature difference is $60^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C} - 20^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C} = 40^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$. Thus, $H_B = \dfrac{K_B A(60 - 20)}{L} = \dfrac{40K_B A}{L}$.

Since the blocks are in series, $H_A = H_B$. Therefore, $\dfrac{20KA}{L} = \dfrac{40K_B A}{L}$.

Simplifying the equation, $20K = 40K_B$, which gives $K_B = \dfrac{20K}{40} = \dfrac{K}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{K}{2}$

25335.text: Let $A = \left\{\dfrac{1967 + 1686isin\theta}{7 - 3icos\theta}: \theta \in R\right\}$. If $A$ contains exactly one positive integer $n$, then the value of $n$ is
25335.sol:
Let $z = \dfrac{1967 + 1686isin\theta}{7 - 3icos\theta}$ is a positive integer.

$⇒ z = \dfrac{\left(1967 + 1686isin\theta\right)\left(7 + 3icos\theta\right)}{\left(7 - 3icos\theta\right)\left(7 + 3icos\theta\right)}$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{1967 \times 7 - 1686 \times 3sin\thetacos\theta + i\left(1686 \times 7sin\theta + 1967 \times 3cos\theta\right)}{49 + 9\cos^{2}\theta}$

Now taking imaginary part as zero we get,

$1686 \times 7sin\theta + 1967 \times 3cos\theta = 0$

$⇒ \left(281 \times 6\right) \times 7sin\theta + \left(281 \times 7\right) \times 3cos\theta = 0$

$⇒ 42sin\theta + 21cos\theta = 0$

$⇒ tan\theta = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \cos^{2}\theta = \dfrac{4}{5} \text{ and } sin\thetacos\theta = - \dfrac{2}{5}$

Now putting the value in $z$we get,

$z = \dfrac{\left(281 \times 7 \times 7\right) - \left(281 \times 6\right) \times 3 \times \left(- \dfrac{2}{5}\right)}{49 + 9 \times \dfrac{4}{5}}$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{281\left(49 + \dfrac{36}{5}\right)}{\left(49 + \dfrac{36}{5}\right)} = 281$

Hence, the value of $n$ is $281$

26429.subject: Physics
26429.text: A projectile is fired from horizontal ground with speed $v$ and projection angle $\theta$. When the acceleration due to gravity is $g$, the range of the projectile is $d$. If at the highest point in its trajectory, the projectile enters a different region where the effective acceleration due to gravity is ${g}^{'} = \dfrac{g}{0 . 81}$, then the new range is ${d}^{'} = nd .$ The value of $n$ is
26429.sol:
Horizontal range of the projectile is $d = \dfrac{{v}^{2}sin2\theta}{g}$

Maximum height attained by the projectile is $H = \dfrac{{v}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}$

So, after entering the new region, time taken by projectile to reach ground

$t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2H}{{g}^{'}}}$$= \sqrt{\dfrac{2\left(\dfrac{{v}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}\right)}{\dfrac{g}{0 . 81}}}$

$= \dfrac{0 . 94vsin\theta}{g}$

So, horizontal displacement done by the projectile in new region is

$x = \dfrac{0 . 9vsin\theta}{g} \times vcos\theta$

$= 0 . 9\dfrac{{v}^{2}sin2\theta}{2g}$

So, new range is ${d}^{'} = \dfrac{d}{2} + x$

$= \dfrac{{v}^{2}sin2\theta}{2g} + 0 . 9\dfrac{{v}^{2}sin2\theta}{2g}$

$= 0 . 95d$

So, $n = 0 . 95d$

29041.subject: Chemistry
29041.text: A first row transition metal $(\mathrm{M})$ does not liberate $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ gas from dilute HCl.1 mol of aqueous solution of $\mathrm{MSO}_{4}$ is treated with excess of aqueous KCN and then $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{~S}(\mathrm{~g})$ is passed through the solution. The amount of MS (metal sulphide) formed from the above reaction is $\_\_\_\_$ mol.
29041.sol:
The first row transition metal (M) that does not liberate $H_2$ gas from dilute $HCl$ is Copper ($Cu$), as it has a positive reduction potential ($E^\circ_{Cu^{2+}/Cu} = +0.34\text{ V}$).
When $1\text{ mol}$ of $CuSO_4$ reacts with excess aqueous $KCN$, it first forms $Cu(CN)_2$, which is unstable and decomposes to $CuCN$ and cyanogen gas $(CN)_2$.
$2CuSO_4 + 4KCN \rightarrow 2Cu(CN)_2 + 2K_2SO_4$
$2Cu(CN)_2 \rightarrow 2CuCN + (CN)_2$
The $CuCN$ then dissolves in excess $KCN$ to form a highly stable soluble complex, potassium tetracyanocuprate(I):
$CuCN + 3KCN \rightarrow K_3[Cu(CN)_4]$
The complex $[Cu(CN)_4]^{3-}$ is so stable that its dissociation constant is extremely low. When $H_2S$ gas is passed through this solution, the concentration of $Cu^+$ ions is insufficient to exceed the solubility product of $Cu_2S$.
Therefore, no precipitate of metal sulphide is formed.
The amount of $MS$ (or $M_2S$) formed is $0\text{ mol}$.

30353.sol:
C-halogen bond length totally depends on the electronegativity difference between Carbon and halogen. The more the difference and the less is the bond length. The electronegativity order of halogens is $I < Br < Cl < F$. Hence, the correct order of increasing C-halogen bond length is $CH3F < CH3Cl < CH3Br < CH3I .$

Or we can say that as the size of halogen increases C-halogen bond length also increases.

Match the List-I with List-II
\(
List-I (Thermodynamic Process)List-II

A.Work done in reversible,
isothermal expansion of
2 mol ideal gas from 2 dm^3
to 20 dm^3 at 300 K		I.4
B.Work done in irreversible

at 300 K against
constant pressure 3 kPa		II.11.5
C.Change in internal energy
for adiabatic expansion of
1 mol ideal gas, $\Delta$T = 320 K,
\overline{C}_V=$\dfrac{3}{2}$R		III.6
D.Change in enthalpy at constant
pressure of
1 mol ideal gas, $\Delta$T = 337 K,
\overline{C}_p=$\dfrac{5}{2}$R		IV.7

32544.sol:

A. Reversible isothermal expansion (2 mol, 2→20 dm³, 300 K):

B. Irreversible isothermal expansion (1 mol, 1→3 m³, 3 kPa constant pressure):
$W = P_{ext}\Delta V = 3000 \times (3-1) = 6000$ J = 6 kJ → III
C. Adiabatic expansion (1 mol, $\Delta T$ = -320 K, $C_V = \frac{3}{2}R$):
$\Delta U = nC_V|\Delta T| = 1 \times \frac{3}{2} \times 8.314 \times 320 = 3,991$ J ≈ 4 kJ → I
D. Enthalpy change (1 mol, $\Delta T$ = 337 K, $C_p = \frac{5}{2}R$):
$\Delta H = nC_p\Delta T = 1 \times \frac{5}{2} \times 8.314 \times 337 = 7,016$ J ≈ 7 kJ → IV

34123.subject: Mathematics
34123.text: The value of the integral $\int\limits_{-1}^{1} \left(\dfrac{x^3 + |x| + 1}{x^2 + 2|x| + 1}\right) dx$ is equal to :
34123.sol:
Let $I = \int_{-1}^{1} \left(\dfrac{x^3 + |x| + 1}{x^2 + 2|x| + 1}\right) dx$

We can split the integral into two parts:

$I = \int_{-1}^{1} \dfrac{x^3}{x^2 + 2|x| + 1} dx + \int_{-1}^{1} \dfrac{|x| + 1}{x^2 + 2|x| + 1} dx$

The first integrand $f(x) = \dfrac{x^3}{x^2 + 2|x| + 1}$ is an odd function since $f(-x) = -f(x)$. Therefore, its integral over the symmetric interval $[-1, 1]$ is zero.

The second integrand $g(x) = \dfrac{|x| + 1}{x^2 + 2|x| + 1}$ is an even function since $g(-x) = g(x)$. Therefore, its integral over $[-1, 1]$ is twice the integral over $[0, 1]$.

$I = 0 + 2 \int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{x + 1}{x^2 + 2x + 1} dx$

$I = 2 \int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{x + 1}{(x + 1)^2} dx$

$I = 2 \int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{1}{x + 1} dx$

$I = 2 [\log_e(x + 1)]_{0}^{1}$

$I = 2(\log_e 2 - \log_e 1) = 2\log_e 2$

Answer: $2\log_e 2$

34134.subject: Mathematics
34134.sol:
Let $f(x) = \log_2(x^2 + 4)$ for $x \ge 0$.

To find the inverse function $f^{-1}(x)$, we set $y = \log_2(x^2 + 4)$ and solve for $x$:

$2^y = x^2 + 4$

$x^2 = 2^y - 4$

$x = \sqrt{2^y - 4}$

Thus, $f^{-1}(x) = \sqrt{2^x - 4}$.

The given expression is $\alpha = \displaystyle\int_0^{2\sqrt{3}} f(x)\,dx + \displaystyle\int_2^4 f^{-1}(x)\,dx$.

We observe the limits of the first integral and evaluate the function at these points:

$f(0) = \log_2(0 + 4) = 2$

$f(2\sqrt{3}) = \log_2((2\sqrt{3})^2 + 4) = \log_2(12 + 4) = \log_2(16) = 4$

These exactly match the limits of the second integral. Using the standard property of definite integrals for inverse functions:

$\displaystyle\int_a^b f(x)\,dx + \displaystyle\int_{f(a)}^{f(b)} f^{-1}(x)\,dx = b f(b) - a f(a)$

Substituting $a = 0$ and $b = 2\sqrt{3}$:

$\alpha = 2\sqrt{3} \cdot f(2\sqrt{3}) - 0 \cdot f(0)$

$\alpha = 2\sqrt{3} \cdot 4 - 0 = 8\sqrt{3}$

Therefore, $\alpha^2 = (8\sqrt{3})^2 = 64 \times 3 = 192$.

Answer: $192$

34832.text: If $y = y ( x )$ is the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = ( tanx - y ) {sec}^{2}x$ , $x \in \left(- \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ , such that $y\left(0\right) = 0$, then $y\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ is equal to:
34832.sol:
The given differential equation can be written as
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y{sec}^{2}x = tanx . {sec}^{2}x$

Hence, solution of given differential equation,

$⇒ y . {e}^{tanx} = tanx . {e}^{tanx} - ∫ se{c}^{2}x . {e}^{tanx}dx$ (using integration by parts)

$⇒ y . {e}^{tanx} = tanx . {e}^{tanx} - {e}^{tanx} + c$

Given, $y\left(0\right) = 0 ⇒ c = 1$

Solution of given differential is

$y . {e}^{tanx} = tanx . {e}^{tanx} - {e}^{tanx} + 1$

Hence, $y\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\left(- 1\right){e}^{- 1} - {e}^{- 1} + 1}{{e}^{- 1}}$

$⇒ y\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = e - 2$

35589.text: If the domain of the function $f(x)=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x-5}{11-3 x}\right)+\sin ^{-1}\left(2 x^{2}-3 x+1\right)$ is the interval $[\alpha, \beta]$, then $\alpha+2 \beta$ is equal to :

For $\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2x-5}{11-3x}\right)$: $-1 \leq \frac{2x-5}{11-3x} \leq 1$ gives $x \leq \frac{16}{5}$ or $x > 6$.
For $\sin^{-1}(2x^2 - 3x + 1)$: $-1 \leq 2x^2 - 3x + 1 \leq 1$.
Lower bound always satisfied (discriminant $< 0$).
Upper bound gives $x(2x-3) \leq 0$, so $0 \leq x \leq \frac{3}{2}$.
Intersection of both conditions: $[0, \frac{3}{2}]$.
Thus $\alpha = 0$, $\beta = \frac{3}{2}$.
$\alpha + 2\beta = 0 + 3 = 3$.

36514.text: The number of ways in which an examiner can assign 30 marks to 8 questions, giving not less than 2 marks to any question, is :

37019.subject: Mathematics
37019.text: Let the sum of the first $n$ terms of an A.P. be $3n^2 + 5n$. Then the sum of squares of the first $10$ terms of the A.P. is:
37019.sol:
Given the sum of the first $n$ terms of the A.P. is $S_n = 3n^2 + 5n$.

The $n$-th term of the A.P. is given by:

$T_n = S_n - S_{n-1}$

$T_n = (3n^2 + 5n) - [3(n-1)^2 + 5(n-1)]$

$T_n = 3n^2 + 5n - [3(n^2 - 2n + 1) + 5n - 5]$

$T_n = 3n^2 + 5n - (3n^2 - 6n + 3 + 5n - 5)$

$T_n = 6n + 2$

We need to find the sum of the squares of the first $10$ terms:

$\sum_{n=1}^{10} T_n^2 = \sum_{n=1}^{10} (6n + 2)^2$

$\sum_{n=1}^{10} T_n^2 = \sum_{n=1}^{10} (36n^2 + 24n + 4)$

$\sum_{n=1}^{10} T_n^2 = 36 \sum_{n=1}^{10} n^2 + 24 \sum_{n=1}^{10} n + \sum_{n=1}^{10} 4$

Using the formulas for the sum of squares and sum of first $n$ natural numbers:

$\sum_{n=1}^{10} T_n^2 = 36 \left( \dfrac{10 \times 11 \times 21}{6} \right) + 24 \left( \dfrac{10 \times 11}{2} \right) + 4 \times 10$

$\sum_{n=1}^{10} T_n^2 = 36(385) + 24(55) + 40$

$\sum_{n=1}^{10} T_n^2 = 13860 + 1320 + 40 = 15220$

Answer: $15220$

$= {\log}_{e}2$

37720.text: Let $R$ be the interior region between the lines $3x - y + 1 = 0 and x + 2y - 5 = 0$ containing the origin. The set of all values of $a$, for which the points $\left({a}^{2}, a + 1\right)$ lie in $R$, is :

$⇒ 3\left({a}^{2}\right) - ( a + 1 ) + 1 > 0$

Using intersection of $\left(i\right)\text{and}\left(ii\right)$,

$⇒ a \in ( - 3, 0 ) ∪ \left(\dfrac{1}{3}, 1\right)$

38650.text: If a unit vector $\overset{\to}{a}$ makes angles $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with $\overset{^}{i}, \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ with $\overset{^}{j}$ and $\theta \in \left(0, \pi\right)$ with $\overset{^}{k},$ then a value of $\theta$ is:

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{2} + \cos^{2}\theta = 1$

$⇒ \cos^{2}\theta = 1 - \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$⇒ \cos^{2}\theta = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ or $\dfrac{2\pi}{3} .$

39607.text: A network of four resistances is connected to $9V$ battery, as shown in figure. The magnitude of voltage difference between the points $A$ and $B$ is __________ $V$.
39607.sol:
The resistance in each branch is $6Ω$. They are in parallel. So, net resistance is $R ' = \dfrac{6}{2} = 3Ω$.

The total current flowing through the loop,

$I = \dfrac{V}{R '} = \dfrac{9V}{3Ω} = 3A$

Thus, through each branch the current is $1 . 5A$.

Hence, the voltage difference across the points is

${V}_{A} - {V}_{B} = \left(4 \times 1 . 5\right) - \left(2 \times 1 . 5\right) = 3V$

41416.subject: Physics
41416.text:
The current passing through a conducting loop in the form of equilateral triangle of side $4 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~cm}$ is 2 A. The magnetic field at its centroid is $\alpha \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~T}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
(Given : $\mu_{\mathrm{o}}=4 \pi \times 10^{-7}$ SI units)
41416.sol:
For an equilateral triangle of side $a$, the distance of the centroid from any side is $r = \frac{a}{2\sqrt{3}}$.
Given side $a = 4\sqrt{3}$ cm $= 4\sqrt{3} \times 10^{-2}$ m.
So, $r = \frac{4\sqrt{3} \times 10^{-2}}{2\sqrt{3}} = 2 \times 10^{-2}$ m.
The magnetic field at the centroid due to one side of the triangle is $B_1 = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} (\sin \theta_1 + \sin \theta_2)$.
For an equilateral triangle, $\theta_1 = \theta_2 = 60^\circ$.
$B_1 = \frac{10^{-7} \times 2}{2 \times 10^{-2}} (\sin 60^\circ + \sin 60^\circ) = 10^{-5} \times (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) = \sqrt{3} \times 10^{-5}$ T.
The total magnetic field at the centroid due to all three sides is $B = 3B_1 = 3\sqrt{3} \times 10^{-5}$ T.
Comparing with $B = \alpha \times 10^{-5}$ T, we get $\alpha = 3\sqrt{3}$.

47300.subject: Biology
47300.text: Choose the correct sequence of wall layers in a microsporangium of an angiosperm.
47300.sol:
A typical microsporangium is generally surrounded by four wall layers. From the outermost to the innermost, the sequence is:

1. Epidermis: The outermost protective layer.
2. Endothecium: The layer just below the epidermis, which helps in dehiscence of the anther.
3. Middle layers: One to three layers of cells that are ephemeral and lie between the endothecium and tapetum.
4. Tapetum: The innermost layer that nourishes the developing pollen grains.

Thus, the correct sequence is Epidermis, Endothecium, Middle layer, Tapetum.

47541.subject: Chemistry
47541.text:
For the following gaseous reversible reaction:
$3\text{A}_{(g)} + \text{B}_{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{A}_3\text{B}_{(g)} \quad (\Delta_r H = -q\text{ kJ})$. The amount of product $\text{A}_3\text{B}_{(g)}$ is affected by ____
47541.sol:
The given reversible reaction is $3\text{A}_{(g)} + \text{B}_{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{A}_3\text{B}_{(g)}$ with $\Delta_r H = -q\text{ kJ}$.

The reaction is exothermic since $\Delta_r H < 0$. According to Le Chatelier's principle, a change in temperature will shift the equilibrium position, thereby affecting the amount of product $\text{A}_3\text{B}_{(g)}$.

The change in the number of gaseous moles is $\Delta n_g = 1 - (3 + 1) = -3$. Since $\Delta n_g \neq 0$, a change in pressure will also shift the equilibrium position, affecting the amount of product.

A catalyst only alters the rate at which equilibrium is attained and does not change the equilibrium composition or the amount of product formed.

Therefore, the amount of product $\text{A}_3\text{B}_{(g)}$ is affected by both temperature and pressure.

Answer: Both temperature and pressure

50404.subject: Physics
50404.text: There are two wires of same material and same length while the diameter of second wire is two times the diameter of the first wire. Then the ratio of extensions produced in the wires by applying same load will be
50404.sol:
The extension produced in a wire is given by the formula:

$\Delta L = \dfrac{FL}{AY}$

Since the material and length are the same, Young's modulus $Y$ and length $L$ are constant. The same load $F$ is applied to both wires. Therefore, the extension is inversely proportional to the cross-sectional area $A$.

$\Delta L \propto \dfrac{1}{A}$

The cross-sectional area $A$ is proportional to the square of the diameter $d$ ($A = \dfrac{\pi d^2}{4}$).

$\Delta L \propto \dfrac{1}{d^2}$

Given that the diameter of the second wire is twice the diameter of the first wire ($d_2 = 2d_1$), the ratio of their extensions is:

$\dfrac{\Delta L_1}{\Delta L_2} = \left(\dfrac{d_2}{d_1}\right)^2$

$\dfrac{\Delta L_1}{\Delta L_2} = \left(\dfrac{2d_1}{d_1}\right)^2 = 4$

The ratio of extensions produced in the wires is $4:1$.

Answer: $4:1$

55268.text: Identify the product obtained when RCN is treated with sodium and alcohol.
55268.sol:
The reduction of alkyl cyanides (nitriles) with sodium and alcohol is known as the Mendius reduction.

In this reaction, the cyano group ($-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$) is reduced to a primary amine group ($-\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$).

$\text{R-C}\equiv\text{N} + 4[\text{H}] \xrightarrow{\text{Na/C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}} \text{R-CH}_2\text{-NH}_2$

The product obtained is a primary amine, $\text{RCH}_2\text{NH}_2$.

Answer: $\text{RCH}_2\text{NH}_2$

58445.subject: Chemistry
58445.text: Which from following polymers is obtained by addition polymerisation method?
58445.sol:
Addition polymerization occurs when monomers join without eliminating small molecules, retaining all atoms from the monomer units in the polymer chain.

Nylon 6 undergoes ring-opening polymerization, a subtype of condensation polymerization involving molecular elimination.

Terylene is a polyester formed via condensation polymerization of ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid with water elimination.

Nylon 6,6 is a polyamide synthesized through condensation polymerization of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid, also eliminating water.

Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene) is produced by addition polymerization of tetrafluoroethene ($\mathrm{CF2=CF2}$), where all monomer atoms are incorporated into the polymer without any byproducts.

The polymer formed by addition polymerization is Teflon.

59913.subject: Chemistry
59913.text: Identify from following the correct set of thermodynamic conditions for the reaction to be spontaneous at all temperature.
59913.sol:
The spontaneity of a reaction is determined by the sign of the Gibbs free energy change, given by $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$, where $\Delta G < 0$ indicates a spontaneous process.

For a reaction to be spontaneous at all temperatures, both terms must contribute negatively to $\Delta G$. When $\Delta H < 0$ and $\Delta S > 0$, the equation becomes $\Delta G = (\text{negative}) - T(\text{positive})$. Since $-T\Delta S$ is always negative under these conditions, $\Delta G$ remains negative regardless of temperature.

In contrast, other combinations show temperature dependence or constant non-spontaneity:
$\Delta H > 0$, $\Delta S > 0$: spontaneous only at high temperatures
$\Delta H < 0$, $\Delta S < 0$: spontaneous only at low temperatures
$\Delta H > 0$, $\Delta S < 0$: non-spontaneous at all temperatures

The condition satisfying spontaneity at all temperatures corresponds to $\Delta H < 0$ and $\Delta S > 0$.

Answer: $\boxed{C}$

60584.subject: Mathematics
60584.text: The area bounded by the curve $\mathrm{y}=x^2+3, \mathrm{y}=x, x=3$ and y -axis is...
60584.sol:
Area Between Curves

The area bounded by $y=x^2+3$, $y=x$, $x=3$, and $x=0$ is determined by the definite integral of the difference between the upper and lower functions over the interval $[0, 3]$.

Since $x^2+3 > x$ for all $x$ (as $x^2 - x + 3$ has discriminant $-11$ and is always positive), the area is computed as:

$A = \int_0^3 [(x^2+3) - x] dx = \int_0^3 (x^2 - x + 3) dx$

Evaluating the integral:

$A = \left[ \frac{x^3}{3} - \frac{x^2}{2} + 3x \right]_0^3 = \left( \frac{27}{3} - \frac{9}{2} + 9 \right) - (0) = 9 - \frac{9}{2} + 9 = \frac{27}{2}$

The area is $\frac{27}{2}$ square units, corresponding to option C.

64076.subject: Mathematics
64076.text: The value of ' $a$ ' so that the sum of squares of the roots of the equation $x^2-(a-2) x-a+1=0$ assumes the least value is
64076.sol:
Given the quadratic equation $x^2 - (a-2)x - a + 1 = 0$ with roots $α$ and $β$, Vieta's formulas yield:

$α + β = a - 2$
$αβ = 1 - a$

The sum of squares of the roots is $S = α^2 + β^2 = (α + β)^2 - 2αβ$.

Substituting the expressions in terms of $a$:

$S = (a - 2)^2 - 2(1 - a) = a^2 - 4a + 4 - 2 + 2a = a^2 - 2a + 2$

This quadratic function $S(a) = a^2 - 2a + 2$ has its minimum at the vertex $a = -(-2)/(2 \cdot 1) = 1$.

The sum of squares of the roots assumes the least value when $a = 1$.

The lines are given by $\overline{r} = (4\hat{i} - \hat{j}) + \lambda(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k})$ and $\overline{r} = (\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}) + \mu(2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - 5\hat{k})$.

The shortest distance between skew lines is found using $d = \frac{|(\overline{a_2} - \overline{a_1}) \cdot (\overline{b_1} \times \overline{b_2})|}{|\overline{b_1} \times \overline{b_2}|}$.

Computing $\overline{a_2} - \overline{a_1} = (\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}) - (4\hat{i} - \hat{j}) = -3\hat{i} + 2\hat{k}$.

The cross product yields $\overline{b_1} \times \overline{b_2} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j}$ with magnitude $\sqrt{5}$.

The scalar triple product is $-6$, so the distance becomes $d = \frac{6}{\sqrt{5}}$.

The shortest distance is $\frac{6}{\sqrt{5}}$ units.

65071.subject: Mathematics
65071.text: If $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ are three vectors such that $\vec{a} \perp (\vec{b} + \vec{c}), \vec{b} \perp (\vec{c} + \vec{a}),$ and $\vec{c} \perp (\vec{a} + \vec{b})$ and $|\vec{a}| = 1, |\vec{b}| = 2, |\vec{c}| = 3$, then $|\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}|$ is...
65071.sol:
Given $\vec{a} \perp (\vec{b} + \vec{c})$, we have $\vec{a} \cdot (\vec{b} + \vec{c}) = 0 \Rightarrow \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = 0$

Similarly, $\vec{b} \perp (\vec{c} + \vec{a}) \Rightarrow \vec{b} \cdot (\vec{c} + \vec{a}) = 0 \Rightarrow \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{a} = 0$

And $\vec{c} \perp (\vec{a} + \vec{b}) \Rightarrow \vec{c} \cdot (\vec{a} + \vec{b}) = 0 \Rightarrow \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{b} = 0$

Adding the above three equations, we get:

$2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}) = 0$

Using the identity for the square of the sum of three vectors:

$|\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}|^2 = |\vec{a}|^2 + |\vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{c}|^2 + 2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a})$

Substituting the given values $|\vec{a}| = 1$, $|\vec{b}| = 2$, and $|\vec{c}| = 3$:

$|\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}|^2 = 1^2 + 2^2 + 3^2 + 0$

$|\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}|^2 = 1 + 4 + 9 = 14$

$|\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}| = \sqrt{14}$

Answer: $\sqrt{14}$

65177.text: $\bar{a}=\hat{i}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}, \overline{\mathrm{b}}=\hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}, \overline{\mathrm{c}}=\hat{\mathrm{k}}-\hat{i}$ then a unit vector $\overline{\mathrm{d}}$ such that $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{d}=0=[\bar{b} \bar{c} \bar{d}]$ is
65177.sol:
Let $\bar{d}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}$ be a unit vector orthogonal to $\bar{a}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}$ and coplanar with $\bar{b}=\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, $\bar{c}=\hat{k}-\hat{i}$.

The orthogonality condition $\bar{a}\cdot\bar{d}=0$ gives $x-y=0$, so $x=y$.

The coplanarity of $\bar{b}$, $\bar{c}$, $\bar{d}$ is equivalent to $\left[\bar{b}\ \bar{c}\ \bar{d}\right]=0$, which implies $\bar{d}$ is orthogonal to $\bar{b}\times\bar{c}$.

Compute $\bar{b}\times\bar{c}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}=\hat{i}(1\cdot1-(-1)\cdot0)-\hat{j}(0\cdot1-(-1)\cdot(-1))+\hat{k}(0\cdot0-1\cdot(-1))=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$.

Then $\bar{d}\cdot(\bar{b}\times\bar{c})=x+y+z=0$. With $x=y$, we get $2x+z=0$, so $z=-2x$.

Thus $\bar{d}=x(\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})$. The unit vector condition requires $|x|\sqrt{1^2+1^2+(-2)^2}=1$, so $|x|\sqrt{6}=1$ and $x=\pm\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}$.

Therefore $\bar{d}=\pm\frac{\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}}{\sqrt{6}}$, which corresponds to Option D.

67032.text: Assuming the drops to be spherical, 27 identical drops of mercury are charged simultaneously to the same potential of 20 volt. If all the charged drops are made to combine to form one big drop, then potential of big drop will be
67032.sol:
Given $n = 27$ small drops, each with radius $r$ and charge $q$, forming a single large drop with radius $R$ and charge $Q$, with the potential of a small drop given as $V_\text{small} = 20\, \text{V}$.

Volume conservation requires $n \cdot \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3$, or $27r^3 = R^3$. Taking the cube root yields $R = 3r$.

Charge conservation gives $Q = nq = 27q$.

The potential of a spherical drop is $V = \frac{kq}{r}$ for small drops, so $20 = \frac{kq}{r}$. For the large drop, $V_\text{big} = \frac{kQ}{R}$.

Substituting $Q = 27q$ and $R = 3r$, $V_\text{big} = \frac{k(27q)}{3r} = 9 \cdot \frac{kq}{r} = 9 \times 20 = 180\, \text{V}$.

The potential of the large drop is $\boxed{180\, \text{V}}$.

67215.text: If earth has a mass nine times and radius twice to the planet P. Then $\dfrac{v_e}{3}\sqrt{x}$ ms^{-1}$ will be the minimum velocity required by a rocket to pull out of gravitational force of P, where $v_e$ is escape velocity on earth. The value of $x$ is$
67215.sol:
The escape velocity on Earth is given by $v_e = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM_e}{R_e}}$

The escape velocity on planet P is given by $v_p = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM_p}{R_p}}$

Given that $M_e = 9M_p \Rightarrow M_p = \dfrac{M_e}{9}$ and $R_e = 2R_p \Rightarrow R_p = \dfrac{R_e}{2}$

Substituting these values into the expression for $v_p$:

$v_p = \sqrt{\dfrac{2G \left( \dfrac{M_e}{9} \right)}{\dfrac{R_e}{2}}}$

$v_p = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM_e}{R_e} \times \dfrac{2}{9}}$

$v_p = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM_e}{R_e}} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}$

$v_p = \dfrac{v_e}{3}\sqrt{2}$

Comparing this with the given expression $\dfrac{v_e}{3}\sqrt{x}$, we get $x = 2$.

Answer: $2$

67650.subject: Physics
67650.text: The magnitude of magnetic induction at mid point 'O' due to current arrangement as shown in figure will be ($\mu_0$ = permeability of free space)
67650.sol:
From the given figure, the horizontal distance between the vertical wire segment BC and the vertical wire segment ET is $a$.

Since point O is the midpoint, the perpendicular distance from O to each of these vertical segments is $a/2$.

Assuming the horizontal wire segments AB and DE are collinear and their extended axis passes through O, the magnetic field produced by them at point O is zero.

The vertical segment BC acts as a semi-infinite straight wire with its end at the level of O. The magnetic induction at O due to BC is $B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi(a/2)} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi a}$. By the right-hand thumb rule, its direction is perpendicular to the plane of the paper, pointing outwards.

The vertical segment ET also acts as a semi-infinite straight wire with its end at the level of O. The magnetic induction at O due to ET is $B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi(a/2)} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi a}$. By the right-hand thumb rule, its direction is also perpendicular to the plane of the paper, pointing outwards.

Since both magnetic fields are in the same direction, the total magnetic induction at O is the sum of their magnitudes:

$B = B_1 + B_2$

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi a} + \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi a} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{\pi a}$

68001.text: Mass and volume of a body are found to be $(6.00 \pm 0.03)$ kg and $(2.00 \pm 0.02)\text{m}^3$ respectively. Then the density of a body is
68001.sol:
Density $\rho = \dfrac{M}{V}$

$\rho = \dfrac{6.00}{2.00} = 3.00 \text{ kg/m}^3$

The maximum fractional error in density is given by

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} = \dfrac{\Delta M}{M} + \dfrac{\Delta V}{V}$

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{3.00} = \dfrac{0.03}{6.00} + \dfrac{0.02}{2.00}$

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{3.00} = 0.005 + 0.010 = 0.015$

$\Delta \rho = 3.00 \times 0.015 = 0.045 \text{ kg/m}^3$

Thus, the density of the body is $(3.00 \pm 0.045) \text{ kg/m}^3$.

68661.text: For a particle performing linear S.H.M. of amplitude 'r', the potential energy is '$\lambda$' times its total energy. The displacement of particle is
68661.sol:
The potential energy of a particle in linear S.H.M. at a displacement $x$ is given by $U = \dfrac{1}{2} m \omega^2 x^2$.

The total energy of the particle with amplitude $r$ is given by $E = \dfrac{1}{2} m \omega^2 r^2$.

According to the given condition, $U = \lambda E$.

Substituting the expressions for $U$ and $E$, we get:

$\dfrac{1}{2} m \omega^2 x^2 = \lambda \left( \dfrac{1}{2} m \omega^2 r^2 \right)$

$x^2 = \lambda r^2$

$x = r \sqrt{\lambda}$

The displacement of the particle is $r \sqrt{\lambda}$.

Answer: $r\sqrt{\lambda}$

69451.text: When the zener diode is used as voltage regulator, it is connected in
options: reverse bias and in series with load.
forward bias and in series with load.
forward bias and in parallel with load.
reverse bias and in parallel with load.
69451.sol:
A Zener diode functions as a voltage regulator by maintaining a constant output voltage across a load during reverse breakdown operation. In this region, the voltage remains stable at $V_Z$ across a wide current range, requiring reverse bias connection.

To regulate load voltage, the diode is connected in parallel with the load, ensuring $V_Z$ appears directly across it. A series resistor limits current and drops excess input voltage.

The correct configuration is therefore reverse bias and parallel connection, making option D the answer.

69483.subject: Physics
69483.text: The resultant logic gate from the combination of following gates is
69483.sol:
Circuit Analysis

The circuit consists of two NOT gates followed by a NOR gate with inputs $A$ and $B$.

The first NOT gate inverts input $A$, producing $A'$.

The second NOT gate inverts input $B$, producing $B'$.

These signals are fed into a NOR gate, yielding output $Y = (A' + B')'$.

Applying De Morgan's theorem, $(X + Y)' = X' \cdot Y'$, so $Y = (A')' \cdot (B')'$.

Since double inversion returns the original variable, $(A')' = A$ and $(B')' = B$, so $Y = A \cdot B$.

This is the Boolean expression for an AND gate.

69765.text: A composite slab consists of two materials having coefficients of thermal conductivity K and 2 K , thickness x and 4 x respectively. The temperatures of two outer surfaces of a composite slab are $T_2 and T_1$ respectively ( $\mathrm{T}_2 \gt \mathrm{T}_1$ ). The rate of heat transfer through the slab in a steady state is $\left[\frac{A\left(T_2-T_1\right) K}{x}\right] f$, where $f$ is equal to
69765.sol:
The thermal resistance for a material is given by $R = \frac{L}{KA}$, where $L$ is thickness, $K$ is thermal conductivity, and $A$ is cross-sectional area.

For material 1 with thickness $x$ and conductivity $K$, $R_1 = \frac{x}{KA}$.

For material 2 with thickness $4x$ and conductivity $2K$, $R_2 = \frac{4x}{2KA} = \frac{2x}{KA}$.

The total resistance for materials in series is $R_{total} = R_1 + R_2 = \frac{x}{KA} + \frac{2x}{KA} = \frac{3x}{KA}$.

Heat transfer rate is $\frac{Q}{t} = \frac{\Delta T}{R_{total}} = \frac{T_2 - T_1}{\frac{3x}{KA}} = \frac{A(T_2 - T_1)K}{3x}$.

Comparing with the given form $\left[\frac{A(T_2-T_1) K}{x}\right] f$, we find $f = \frac{1}{3}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

70524.subject: Physics
70524.text: The frequency of fourth overtone of a closed pipe is in unison with the fifth overtone of an open pipe. The ratio of length of closed pipe to that of open pipe is
70524.sol:
The fourth overtone of a closed pipe is in unison with the fifth overtone of an open pipe, so their frequencies are equal.

For a closed pipe, the $n^{\text{th}}$ overtone has frequency $f_c = (2n+1)\frac{v}{4L_c}$. Setting $n=4$ gives $f_{c} = 9\frac{v}{4L_c}$.

For an open pipe, the $n^{\text{th}}$ overtone has frequency $f_o = (n+1)\frac{v}{2L_o}$. With $n=5$, $f_o = 6\frac{v}{2L_o}$.

Equating the frequencies yields:

$9\frac{v}{4L_c} = 6\frac{v}{2L_o}$

Cancel $v$ and simplify:

$\frac{9}{4L_c} = \frac{3}{L_o}$

Rearranging gives $\frac{L_c}{L_o} = \frac{9}{4} \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{3}{4}$.

The ratio of lengths is $L_c : L_o = 3 : 4$.

71942.subject: Chemistry
71942.text: What is the packing efficiency in BCC unit cell ?
71942.sol:
In a body-centered cubic (BCC) unit cell, the atoms touch each other along the body diagonal.

Let the edge length of the unit cell be $a$ and the radius of the atom be $r$.

The length of the body diagonal is $\sqrt{3}$a$.

Since the atoms touch along the body diagonal, we have:

\sqrt{3}a = 4r \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{4r}{\sqrt{3}}$

The number of atoms per unit cell in a BCC structure is $Z = 2$.

Volume of the unit cell is $V = a^3 = \left(\dfrac{4r}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^3 = \dfrac{64r^3}{3\sqrt{3}}$

Volume occupied by the atoms is $v = 2 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \dfrac{8}{3}\pi r^3$

Packing efficiency is given by:

$\text{Packing efficiency} = \dfrac{v}{V} \times 100$

$\text{Packing efficiency} = \dfrac{\dfrac{8}{3}\pi r^3}{\dfrac{64r^3}{3\sqrt{3}}} \times 100 = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}\pi}{8} \times 100$

Substituting the values of $\pi$ and $\sqrt{3}:

\text{Packing efficiency} \approx 68\ \%$

Answer: $68\ \%$

72198.subject: Physics
72198.text: The electric field at a point in a certain region of free space due to a charge Q is 0. The electric potential at that point is
options: directly proportional to the charge Q.
72198.sol:
The electric field due to a point charge $Q$ at a distance $r$ is given by $E = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{Q}{r^2}$.

Given that the electric field $E = 0$, this implies that the distance $r \to \infty$ (assuming $Q \neq 0$).

The electric potential due to the charge $Q$ at a distance $r$ is given by $V = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{Q}{r}$.

76899.subject: Mathematics
76899.text: If $M=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$, then what is the value of $|M|\,|\text{adj}M|$ ?
76899.sol:
Given $M = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$

The determinant of the diagonal matrix $M$ is $|M| = 2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8$.

For a square matrix of order $n$, the determinant of its adjoint is given by $|\text{adj}M| = |M|^{n-1}$.

Since the order of $M$ is $n = 3$, we have $|\text{adj}M| = |M|^{3-1} = |M|^2$.

The required value is $|M| \, |\text{adj}M| = |M| \times |M|^2 = |M|^3$.

Substituting $|M| = 8$, we get $8^3 = 512$.

Answer: $512$

options: Originate in the lumen of vessels
Are extensions of xylem parenchyma cells into vessels
Are linked to the ascent of sap through xylem vessels
79376.sol:
Tyloses are balloon-shaped structures in xylem vessels developed by xylem parenchyma cells.



Malpighi (1686) for the first time reported the ‘balloon-shaped sacs’ in the lumen of vessels of heartwood and he named it as tyloses based on the Greek word ‘Thyllen’ meaning ‘bag’ or ‘container’. Tyloses development occurs through the pit-pairs connecting parenchyma and tracheids or vessels. Sometimes many tyloses originate from a single parenchymatous cell. The tyloses completely fill the lumen rich in the tracheids and vessels of heartwood than sapwood.

On integrating, we get,
$\dfrac{y^{2}}{2} - 2xy + y - \dfrac{x^{2}}{2} + 3x + C = 0$
Since, the curve passes through $\left(1,1\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} - 2 + 1 - \dfrac{1}{2} + 3 + C = 0$
$C = - 2$
$y^{2} - 4xy + 2y - x^{2} + 6x - 4 = 0$~or& $x^{2} + 4xy + y^{2} - 6x - 2y + 4 = 0$

91686.text: A man alternately tosses a coin and throw a dice, beginning with the coin. The probability that he gets a head in coin before he gets a $5$ or $6$ in dice, is
91686.sol:
$A =$ coin show head
$B =$ dice show $5$ or $6$
$P\left(A\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}, P\left(B\right) = \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}$
Hence, the required Probability $= P\left(A\right) + P\left(A^{C}\right)P\left(B^{C}\right)P\left(A\right) + {\left(P\left(A^{C}\right)P\left(B^{C}\right)\right)}^{2}P\left(A\right) + \ldots$
$= \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{2} + {\left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{2}{3}\right)}^{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} + \ldots$
$= \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{3}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}}{\dfrac{2}{3}} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

91747.subject: Mathematics
91747.text: $The number of real solutions of the equation \sqrt{x + 14 - 8\sqrt{x - 2}} + \sqrt{x + 23 - 10\sqrt{x - 2}} = 3$& are
91747.sol:
The given equation is
$\sqrt{{\left(\sqrt{\text{x} - 2} - 4\right)}^{2}} + \sqrt{{\left(\sqrt{\text{x} - 2} - 5\right)}^{2}} = 3$
$⇒ \left|\sqrt{\text{x} - 2} - 4\right| + \left|\sqrt{\text{x} - 2} - 5\right| = 3$
Put $\sqrt{\text{x} - 2} = \text{y}$

Then, the given equation becomes $\left|\text{y} - 4\right| + \left|\text{y} - 5\right| = 3$
Case $1: \text{y} < 4 ⇒ - \text{y} + 4 - \text{y} + 5 = 3$
$⇒ - 2\text{y} = - 6 ⇒ \text{y} = 3$
Case $2: 4 \le \text{y} < 5 ⇒ \text{y} - 4 - \text{y} + 5 = 3$

$⇒ 1 = 3 ⇒$ no solution
Case $3:$~$\text{y} \ge 5 ⇒ \text{y} - 4 + \text{y} - 5 = 3$
$⇒ 2\text{y} = 12 ⇒ \text{y} = 6$
$\text{y} = 3 ⇒ \sqrt{\text{x} - 2} = 3 ⇒ \text{x} - 2 = 9 ⇒ \text{x} = 11$
$\text{y} = 6 ⇒ \sqrt{\text{x} - 2} = 6 ⇒ \text{x} - 2 = 36 ⇒ \text{x} = 38$
$⇒ \text{x} = 11$ and 38 i.e. two solutions.

94043.text: Assuming that four protons combine to form a helium nucleus and two positrons each of mass $0. 000549a. m. u.$, calculate the energy released. Given, the mass of ${}_{1}H^{1} = 1.007825a. m. u.$ and mas of ${}_{2}{He}^{4}= 4. 002603a. m. u.$

$Q = $\l$ left[14{m}_{N} \left(1H^{1}\right) - {m}_{N}\left(2{He}^{4}\right) - 2{m}_{e}\right]\times931.5$ MeV .....(i)

Where ${m}_{e}$ represents the mass of the positron $\left({}_{1}e^{0}\right)$ .

Here, ${m}_{N}\left(2{He}^{4}\right)4.002603a . m . u .$; ${m}_{e} = 0.0005499a . m . u .

94576.sol:
Given, $pT^{2}$ = constant

$∴ \left(\dfrac{nRT}{V}\right)T^{2} =$ constant

or $T^{3}V^{- 1} =$ constant

Differentiating the equation, we get

$\dfrac{3T^{2}}{V} . dT - \dfrac{T^{3}}{V^{2}} . dV = 0$

or $3 . dT = \dfrac{T}{V} . dV$

From the equation, $dV = VγdT$

$γ =$ coefficient of volume expansion of gas

$=\dfrac{dV}{V . dT}$

$∴ γ = \dfrac{dV}{V . dT} = \dfrac{3}{T}$

100575.text: A particle of mass \(m\) is at rest at the origin at time \(t=0\) It is subjected to a force, \(F(t)=F_0 e^{-b t}\) in the \(x\)-direction. Its speed \(v(t)\) is depicted by which of the following curves?
100575.sol:
Given \($\mathrm{F}(\mathrm{t})=\mathrm{FO} \mathrme^{-\mathrm{bt}}$\), acceleration \($\mathrm{a}(\mathrm{t})=\mathrm{F}(\mathrm{t})$/ $\mathrm{m}=(\mathrm{FO}$/ $\mathrm{m}) \mathrme^{-\mathrm{bt}}$\),
so \(dv/dt=($\mathrm{FO}$/ $\mathrm{m}) \mathrme^{-\mathrm{bt}}$\).
Integrating with \($\mathrm{v}($0)=0\) gives \($\mathrm{v}(\mathrm{t})=(\mathrm{FO}$/($\mathrm{mb}))\left[$1-\mathrme^{-$\mathrm{bt}$}\right]\).
This rises from 0 and asymptotically approaches \($\mathrm{FO}$/($\mathrm{mb})$\).
Hence the correct \($\mathrm{v}-\mathrm{t}$\) curve is a rising exponential saturating at \($\mathrm{FO}$/($\mathrm{mb})$\), which corresponds to (b).

100814.text:
In the List-I below, four different paths of a particle are given as functions of time. In these functions, $\alphaand\beta$ are positive constants of appropriate dimensions and $\alpha \ne \beta$ . In each case, the force acting on the particle is either zero or conservative. In List-II, five physical quantities of the particle are mentioned: $\overset{\to}{p}$ is the linear momentum, $\overset{\to}{L}$ is the angular momentum about the origin, K is the kinetic energy, U is the potential energy and E is the total energy. Match each path in List-I with those quantities in List-II, which are conserved for that path.
  LIST -I   LIST-II
A) $\overset{\to}{r}\left(t\right) = \alphat\overset{^}{i} + \beta\overset{^}{j}$ P) $\overset{\to}{p}$
B) $\overset{\to}{r}\left(t\right) = \alphacos ⁡ \omegat\overset{^}{i} + \betasin ⁡ \omegat\overset{^}{j}$ Q) $\overset{\to}{L}$
C) $\overset{\to}{r}\left(t\right) = \alphacos ⁡ \omegat\overset{^}{i} + sin ⁡ \omegat\overset{^}{j}$ R) $K$
D) $\overset{\to}{r}\left(t\right) = \alphat\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{\beta}{2}{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j}$ S) $U$
    T) $E$
100814.sol:
$( i )$ $\overset{\to}{r}\left(t\right) = \alphat\overset{^}{i} + \betat\overset{^}{j}$
$\overset{\to}{v} = \dfrac{d\overset{\to}{r}\left(t\right)}{dt} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + \beta\overset{^}{j}$ {constant}
$\overset{\to}{a} = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{dv}}{dt} = 0$
$\overset{\to}{P} = m\overset{\to}{v}$ (remain constant)
$k = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$ {remain constant}
$\overset{\to}{F} = - \left[\dfrac{∂ U}{∂ x}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{∂ U}{∂ y}\overset{^}{i}\right] = 0$
$⇒ U \to$ constant
$E = K + U$
$\dfrac{d\overset{\to}{L}}{dt} = - \overset{\to}{τ} = \overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{F} = 0$
$\overset{\to}{L} =$ constant
$( ii )$ $\overset{\to}{r} = \alphacos ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{i} + \betasin ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{j}$
$\overset{\to}{v} = \dfrac{d\overset{\to}{r}}{dt} = - \alpha\omegasin ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{i} + \beta\omegacos ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{j}$
$\overset{\to}{a} = \dfrac{d\overset{\to}{v}}{dt} = - \alpha{\omega}^{2}cos ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{i} + \beta\omegasin ⁡ ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{j}$
$= - {\omega}^{2}\left[\alphacos ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{i} + \betasin ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{j}\right]$
$\overset{\to}{a} = = - \alpha{\omega}^{2}$
$\overset{\to}{τ} = \overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{F} = 0\left\{\overset{\to}{r}and\overset{\to}{F}areparallel\right\}$
$∆ U = - ∫ F . dr + {∫}_{0}^{r}m{\omega}^{2} . r . dr$
$∆ U = m{\omega}^{2}\left[\dfrac{{r}^{2}}{2}\right]$
$U ∝ {r}^{2}$
$r = \sqrt{{\alpha}^{2}\cos^{2} ⁡ \left(\omegat\right) + {\beta}^{2}\sin^{2} ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)}$
R is a function of time (t)
U depends on r hence it will change with time
Total energy remain constant because force is central
$( iii )$ $\overset{\to}{r}\left(t\right) = \alpha\left(cos ⁡ \omegat\overset{^}{i} + sin ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{j}\right)$
$\overset{\to}{v}\left(t\right) = \dfrac{d\overset{\to}{r}\left(t\right)}{dt} = \alpha\left[- \omegasin ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{i} + \omegacos ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{j}\right]$
$\left|\overset{\to}{v}\right| = \alpha\omega$ (Speed remains constant)
$\overset{\to}{a}\left(t\right) = \dfrac{d\overset{\to}{v}\left(t\right)}{dt} = \alpha\left[- {\omega}^{2}cos ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{i} + {\omega}^{2}sin ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{j}\right]$
$= - \alpha{\omega}^{2}\left[cos ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{i} + sin ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{j}\right]$
$\overset{\to}{a}\left(t\right) = - {\omega}^{2}\left(\overset{\to}{r}\right)$
$\left|\overset{\to}{r}\right| = \alpha$ (remain constant)
Force is central in nature and distance from fixed point is constant.
Potential energy remains constant
Kinetic energy is also constant (speed is constant)
$( iv )$ $\overset{\to}{r} = \alphat\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{\beta}{2}{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j}$
$\overset{\to}{v} = \dfrac{d\overset{\to}{r}}{dt} = \alphat\overset{^}{i} + \betat\overset{^}{j}$ (speed of particle depends on 't')
$\overset{\to}{a} = \dfrac{d\overset{\to}{v}}{dt} = \beta\overset{^}{j}\left\{constant\right\}$
$\overset{\to}{F} = m\overset{\to}{a}\left\{constant\right\}$
$∆ U = - ∫ \overset{\to}{F} . d\overset{\to}{r} = - m{∫}_{0}^{t}\beta\overset{^}{j} . \left(\alpha\overset{^}{i} + \betat\overset{^}{j}\right)dt$
$U = \dfrac{- m{\beta}^{2}{t}^{2}}{2}$
$k = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m\left({\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2}{t}^{2}\right)$
$E = k + U = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\alpha}^{2}$ [remain constant]

102452.subject: Physics
102452.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A simple pendulum of length $1$ m will have a longer time period on the surface of the Moon than on the surface of the Earth.
Reason (R): The time period of a simple pendulum is directly proportional to the square root of its effective length.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
102452.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: The time period of a simple pendulum is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}$. Since the acceleration due to gravity ($g$) on the Moon is less than that on the Earth, the time period ($T$) will be longer on the Moon for the same length of the pendulum.

Reason (R) is true: From the formula $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}$, it is clear that the time period is directly proportional to the square root of its effective length ($T \propto \sqrt{L}$).

However, Reason (R) does not explain Assertion (A). The correct explanation for the longer time period on the Moon is the inverse proportionality of the time period to the square root of the acceleration due to gravity ($T \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{g}}$), not its dependence on length.

Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

103693.text:
A wire carrying a current of $6\text{ A}$ is bent into a circular arc of radius $2\text{ cm}$. If the arc subtends an angle of $120^{\circ}$ at the centre of curvature, the magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre is:
(Take permeability of free space as $4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T m A}^{-1}$)
103693.sol:
The magnetic field at the centre of a circular arc subtending an angle $\theta$ is given by a fraction of the field of a complete circular loop:

$B = \left(\dfrac{\theta}{360^{\circ}}\right) \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$

Given:
$\theta = 120^{\circ}$
$I = 6\text{ A}$
$R = 2\text{ cm} = 0.02\text{ m}$

Substituting the values:
$B = \left(\dfrac{120^{\circ}}{360^{\circ}}\right) \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 6}{2 \times 0.02}$

$B = \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) \dfrac{24\pi \times 10^{-7}}{0.04}$

$B = \dfrac{8\pi \times 10^{-7}}{0.04}$

$B = 200\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}$

$B = 20\pi \times 10^{-6}\text{ T} = 20\pi \mu\text{T}$

Answer: $20\pi \mu\text{T}$

108974.subject: Chemistry
108974.text:
For the synthesis of sulphur trioxide gas represented by the equation $2\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g})$, the forward reaction rate constant is $1.5 \times 10^3$ and the backward reaction rate constant is $3.0 \times 10^2$ at $300\text{ K}$.

[Given: $\mathrm{R} = \dfrac{1}{12}\text{ L atm K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]

The value of $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}$ for this reaction at $300\text{ K}$ is:
108974.sol:
The equilibrium constant in terms of concentration, $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$, is the ratio of the forward rate constant to the backward rate constant:
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}} = \dfrac{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}}} = \dfrac{1.5 \times 10^3}{3.0 \times 10^2} = 5$

For the reaction $2\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g})$, the change in the number of moles of gaseous species is:
$\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}} = \text{moles of gaseous products} - \text{moles of gaseous reactants}$
$\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}} = 2 - (2 + 1) = -1$

The relationship between $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}$ and $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$ is:
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}} = \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}}}$

Substituting the given values:
$\mathrm{RT} = \dfrac{1}{12} \times 300 = 25$
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}} = 5 \times (25)^{-1} = \dfrac{5}{25} = 0.2$

Answer: 0.2

111879.subject: Chemistry
111879.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): tert-Butyl carbocation is highly stable compared to methyl carbocation.
Reason (R): Methyl groups cannot participate in the resonance (mesomeric) effect as they lack $\pi$ bonds or lone pairs of electrons.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
111879.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct: The tert-butyl carbocation, $(CH_3)_3C^{+}$, is a tertiary carbocation and is highly stable compared to the methyl carbocation, $CH_3^{+}$.

Reason (R) is correct: The resonance (mesomeric) effect involves the delocalization of $\pi$ electrons or lone pairs. Methyl groups ($-CH_3$) only have $\sigma$ bonds and lack $\pi$ bonds or lone pairs, so they cannot participate in resonance.

However, (R) is not the correct explanation of (A). The correct explanation for the high stability of the tert-butyl carbocation is that the three methyl groups stabilize the positive charge through hyperconjugation (due to the presence of 9 $\alpha$-hydrogens) and the $+I$ (inductive) effect.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

111896.text:
Match List I with List II.

(A)$CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_2-CH(Cl)-CH(Cl)-CH_3$(I)2-ethylpen\tan^{-1}-ol
(B)$CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH(CH_2OH)-CH_2-CH_3$(II)4-hydroxypentan-2-one
(C)$CH_3-CO-CH_2-CH(OH)-CH_3$(III)pent-1-en-4-yne
(D)$CH_2=CH-CH_2-C \equiv CH$(IV)5-bromo-2,3-dichlorohexane

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
111896.sol:
(A) $CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_2-CH(Cl)-CH(Cl)-CH_3$: Numbering from right to left gives locants 2, 3, 5. Numbering from left to right gives 2, 4, 5. The lowest locant set is 2, 3, 5. Substituents are listed alphabetically. The name is 5-bromo-2,3-dichlorohexane. Matches with (IV).

(B) $CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH(CH_2OH)-CH_2-CH_3$: The principal functional group is -OH. The parent chain must include the carbon attached to the -OH group, even if it is not the longest continuous chain in the molecule. The longest chain containing the -OH group has 5 carbons. Numbering starts from the -OH end. The name is 2-ethylpen\tan^{-1}-ol. Matches with (I).

(C) $CH_3-CO-CH_2-CH(OH)-CH_3$: The ketone group has higher priority than the alcohol group. Numbering starts from the left to give the ketone the lowest locant (2). The name is 4-hydroxypentan-2-one. Matches with (II).

(D) $CH_2=CH-CH_2-C \equiv CH$: Numbering from either side gives locants 1 and 4 for the multiple bonds. In case of a tie, the double bond gets priority for the lower locant. Numbering is from left to right. The name is pent-1-en-4-yne. Matches with (III).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)

112666.subject: Chemistry
112666.text: Benzene reacts with carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride in the presence of anhydrous aluminum chloride and cuprous chloride to form compound $\text{X}$. When compound $\text{X}$ is heated with concentrated sodium hydroxide, it yields two compounds, $\text{Y}$ and $\text{Z}$. The compounds $\text{Y}$ and $\text{Z}$ are respectively:
112666.sol:
The reaction of benzene with carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$) and hydrogen chloride ($\text{HCl}$) in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ and $\text{CuCl}$ is the Gattermann-Koch reaction. The product $\text{X}$ formed is benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$).

Benzaldehyde does not contain any $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms. When heated with a concentrated alkali like concentrated $\text{NaOH}$, aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-hydrogens undergo the Cannizzaro reaction. This is a disproportionation reaction where one molecule of the aldehyde is reduced to the corresponding alcohol and another is oxidized to the salt of the corresponding carboxylic acid.

Therefore, benzaldehyde disproportionates to yield benzyl alcohol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) and sodium benzoate ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COONa}$).

Thus, compounds $\text{Y}$ and $\text{Z}$ are sodium benzoate and benzyl alcohol.

Option (1) is incorrect because it assumes $\text{X}$ is phenol. Option (2) is incorrect because it assumes a simple acid-base neutralization or complete oxidation. Option (4) is incorrect because sodium formate would be a product of a cross-Cannizzaro reaction with formaldehyde.

Answer: Sodium benzoate and benzyl alcohol

117762.subject: Chemistry
117762.text: The absorption maxima for three octahedral complexes $[\text{M}(\text{L}_1)_6]^{3+}$, $[\text{M}(\text{L}_2)_6]^{3+}$ and $[\text{M}(\text{L}_3)_6]^{3+}$ are observed at $450\text{ nm}$, $650\text{ nm}$ and $550\text{ nm}$ respectively. The correct increasing order of the ligand field strength of $\text{L}_1$, $\text{L}_2$ and $\text{L}_3$ is:
117762.sol:
The crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_o$) is equal to the energy of the light absorbed by the coordination complex.

The energy of the absorbed light is inversely proportional to its wavelength ($\lambda$), given by the relation $E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$.

A stronger field ligand causes a larger crystal field splitting ($\Delta_o$), which means the complex will absorb light of higher energy and shorter wavelength.

The given absorption wavelengths are:
$\text{L}_1 = 450\text{ nm}$
$\text{L}_2 = 650\text{ nm}$
$\text{L}_3 = 550\text{ nm}$

The order of wavelengths is $\text{L}_1 < \text{L}_3 < \text{L}_2$.

Therefore, the increasing order of crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_o$) and the ligand field strength is $\text{L}_2 < \text{L}_3 < \text{L}_1$.

Answer: $\text{L}_2 < \text{L}_3 < \text{L}_1$

117770.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In aqueous solution, $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ is strongly reducing while $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ is strongly oxidising, despite both having a $d^{4}$ electronic configuration.

Reason (R): The $d^{3}$ configuration of $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ is highly stable due to a half-filled $t_{2g}$ level, whereas the $d^{5}$ configuration of $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ is highly stable due to an exactly half-filled $d$-subshell.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
117770.sol:
Assertion (A) is true. Both $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ have a $d^{4}$ configuration. $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ acts as a reducing agent because it gets oxidised to $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$. $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ acts as an oxidising agent because it gets reduced to $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$.

Reason (R) is true and correctly explains the Assertion. In an aqueous medium, the $d^{3}$ configuration of $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ is exceptionally stable due to a half-filled $t_{2g}$ set of orbitals in an octahedral crystal field. On the other hand, $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ has a $d^{5}$ configuration, which is extra stable due to a symmetrical half-filled $d$-subshell. This difference in the stability of their product states drives their opposite redox behaviours.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

119275.subject: Chemistry
119275.text: Which of the following compounds CANNOT be obtained as a product from the base-catalyzed aldol condensation reaction between 2-butanone and 4-methylbenzaldehyde (p-tolualdehyde) upon heating?
119275.sol:
The reaction is a base-catalyzed aldol condensation between 2-butanone and 4-methylbenzaldehyde.

2-butanone ($CH_3-CO-CH_2-CH_3$) has two different types of $\alpha$-hydrogens, located at C1 and C3. Thus, it can form two different enolates under basic conditions.

1. If the enolate forms at C1, it attacks the carbonyl carbon of 4-methylbenzaldehyde. Subsequent dehydration yields the cross-aldol product 1-(4-methylphenyl)pent-1-en-3-one.

2. If the enolate forms at C3, it attacks 4-methylbenzaldehyde, and dehydration yields the cross-aldol product 3-methyl-4-(4-methylphenyl)but-3-en-2-one.

3. 2-butanone can also undergo self-aldol condensation. For example, the C1 enolate can attack the carbonyl carbon of another molecule of 2-butanone, leading to 5-methylhept-4-en-3-one after dehydration.

In all valid aldol condensation products, the newly formed double bond is conjugated with the carbonyl group, forming an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated system.

The compound 5-(4-methylphenyl)pent-4-en-2-one has a double bond that is $\beta,\gamma$ to the carbonyl group. Forming this product would require enolate formation at the C4 position of 2-butanone, which is a $\beta$-carbon and lacks acidic protons. Therefore, this unconjugated product cannot be obtained from the reaction.

Answer: 5-(4-methylphenyl)pent-4-en-2-one

119297.subject: Chemistry
119297.text: When 3-pentanone is reacted with benzaldehyde in the presence of dilute NaOH and heat, a major cross-aldol product 'P' is formed. Compound 'P' is then subjected to reductive ozonolysis ($O_3$ followed by $Zn/H_2O$). Identify the two final products formed after ozonolysis.
119297.sol:
The first step is a cross-aldol condensation between 3-pentanone and benzaldehyde.

3-Pentanone ($CH_3-CH_2-CO-CH_2-CH_3$) is a symmetrical ketone with $\alpha$-hydrogens at C2 and C4. In the presence of dilute NaOH, it forms an enolate at C2.

This enolate acts as a nucleophile and attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of benzaldehyde ($C_6H_5-CHO$).

Heating the reaction mixture causes the intermediate $\beta$-hydroxy ketone to undergo dehydration (loss of a water molecule), forming the $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone 'P'. The structure of 'P' is 1-phenyl-2-methylpent-1-en-3-one ($C_6H_5-CH=C(CH_3)-CO-CH_2-CH_3$).

The second step is the reductive ozonolysis of compound 'P' using $O_3$ followed by $Zn/H_2O$.

Ozonolysis cleaves the carbon-carbon double bond ($C=C$). The carbon atom attached to the phenyl ring becomes an aldehyde group, yielding benzaldehyde ($C_6H_5-CHO$).

The other carbon atom of the double bond, which is already part of the ketone chain, is oxidized to a ketone group. This converts the remaining fragment into pentane-2,3-dione ($CH_3-CH_2-CO-CO-CH_3$).

Therefore, the final products are benzaldehyde and pentane-2,3-dione.

Answer: Benzaldehyde and pentane-2,3-dione

120855.subject: Chemistry
120855.text:
Observe the following statements.
I. Sucrose has glycosidic linkage.
II. Cellulose is present in both plants and animals.
III. Lactose contains D-galactose and D-glucose units.
Which of the following statements are correct?
120855.sol:
Let's evaluate each statement to determine which are correct.
- Statement I: Sucrose has a glycosidic linkage. This is correct. Sucrose is a disaccharide formed by a glycosidic linkage between a glucose unit and a fructose unit.
- Statement II: Cellulose is present in both plants and animals. This is incorrect. Cellulose is the main structural component of the primary cell wall of green plants, but it's not present in animals. Animals lack the enzyme cellulase to break down cellulose.
- Statement III: Lactose contains D-galactose and D-glucose units. This is correct. Lactose is a disaccharide commonly known as milk sugar. It's composed of one molecule of Dgalactose and one molecule of D-glucose, joined by a \(\beta\)-1,4-glycosidic linkage.
Therefore, the correct statements are I and III. The correct option is (4).

121350.text: What are the type of sexual spores produced by Ascomycetes?
121350.sol: Commonly known as sac-fungi, the ascomycetes are mostly multicellular, e.g., Penicillium, or rarelyunicellular, e.g., yeast (Saccharomyces). They are saprophytic, decomposers, parasitic or coprophilous (growing on dung). Mycelium is branched and septate. The asexual spores are conidia produced exogenously on the special mycelium called conidiophores. Conidia on germination produce mycelium. <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> Sexual spores are called ascospores</mark>which are produced endogenously in sac like asci (singular ascus). These asci are arranged in different types of fruiting bodies called ascocarps. Some examples are Aspergillus, Claviceps and Neurospora. Neurospora is used extensively in biochemical and genetic work. Manymembers like morels and truffles are edible and are considered delicacies.

123631.subject: Botany
123631.text: What is the function of Mitosis?
options: To segregate duplicated chromosomes into daughter nuclei
To divide the cell itself into two daughter cells
123631.sol: Mitosis accomplishes not only the segregation of duplicated chromosomes into daughter nuclei (karyokinesis), but the cell itself is divided into two daughter cells by the separation of cytoplasm called cytokinesis at the end of which cell division gets completed. In an animal cell, this is achieved by the appearance of a furrow in the plasma membrane. The furrow gradually deepens and ultimately joins in the centre dividing the cell cytoplasm into two. Plant cells however, are enclosed by a relatively inextensible cell wall, thererfore they undergo cytokinesis by a different mechanism. In plant cells, wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls. The formation of the new cell wall begins with the formation of a simple precursor, called the cell-plate that represents the middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells.

127073.sol: DDT or dichloro-diphenyl trichloroethane was the first important synthetic pesticide (organo chlorine) discovered in 1939 by a Swiss chemist Paul Muller. 128101.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In cockroach, the gizzard acts as an efficient grinding mill for food particles.
Reason (R): The gizzard has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and a thick inner cuticle forming six highly chitinous plates called teeth.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
128101.sol:
In the alimentary canal of a cockroach, the crop is followed by the gizzard or proventriculus. The gizzard helps in grinding the food particles, making the Assertion true.

This grinding action is structurally supported by its anatomy: it possesses an outer layer of thick circular muscles and a thick inner cuticle that forms six highly chitinous plates known as teeth. This makes the Reason true.

Because the structural features described in the Reason directly enable the grinding function stated in the Assertion, the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

129547.subject: Zoology
129547.text: How does an increase in body fluid volume affect the release of ADH?
129547.sol: Osmoreceptors in the body are activated by changes in blood volume, body fluid volume and ionic concentration. An excessive loss of fluid from the body can activate these receptors which stimulate the hypothalamus to release antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or vasopressin from the neurohypophysis. ADH facilitates water reabsorption from latter parts of the tubule, thereby preventing diuresis. An increase in body fluid volume can switch off the osmoreceptors and suppress the ADH release to complete the feedback. ADH can also affect the kidney function by its constrictory effects on blood vessels. This causes an increase in blood pressure. An increase in blood pressure can increase the glomerular blood flow and thereby the GFR.

130596.sol: Surgical methods, also called sterilisation, are generally advised for the male/female partner as a terminal method to prevent any more pregnancies. 130912.subject: Zoology
130912.text: What is the role of the corpus luteum in the menstrual cycle?
130912.sol: The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone which is essential for maintenance of the endometrium. Such an endometrium is necessary for implantation of the fertilized ovum and other events of pregnancy. During pregnancy all events of the menstrual cycle stop and there is no menstruation. In the absence of fertilisation, the corpus luteum degenerates. This causes disintegration of the endometrium leading to menstruation, marking a new cycle. In human beings, menstrual cycles ceases around 50 years of age; that is termed as menopause. Cyclic menstruation is an indicator of normal reproductive phase and extends between menarche and menopause.
